QUOTE: `#ifndef MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member #else #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member #endif` and "Library code writes `ctx->state` directly... Consumers who define `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` themselves get the same access" and "Code that writes `ssl->state` against the public header fails to compile"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that defining the macro yields plain member names while ordinary consumers of the public headers see the `private_`-prefixed names.
